mainTopic: The זב with two sightings and ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״; the differences between a מצורע מוסגר and a מצורע מוחלט and their sources in the פסוקים; and the language rules for ספרים versus תפילין ומזוזות.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא. The ברייתא uses the שומרת יום כנגד יום to show that logic cannot prove a זב with two sightings must count seven clean days, so it learns this from the word ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ instead. רב פפא asks אביי how the same word can include him here but exclude him from bringing a קרבן. אביי answers that an excluding word here would teach nothing, and the word is not needed for any other lesson. Next comes a new משנה: a מצורע מוסגר and a מצורע מוחלט differ only in פריעה and פרימה, and when they become pure, only in תגלחת and צפרים. The גמרא searches for the פסוקים behind each difference. רבא rejects a proof from ״וְטָהֵר״ and learns from ״אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ הַנֶּגַע״ instead. He uses ״כׇּל יְמֵי״ to keep the מוסגר included in שילוח, and אביי learns from ״נִרְפָּא״ that the מוסגר is free from shaving and birds. A final משנה teaches that ספרים may be written in any language, while תפילין ומזוזות must be written in אשורית. The גמרא then raises a contradiction from a ברייתא, and רבא begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The woman who waits one day disproves the logical argument
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the idea that a two-sighting זב must count seven just because he makes a bed and seat impure. A שומרת יום כנגד יום also makes them impure, yet she does not count seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who waits one clean day for one day of bleeding proves the point. She makes a bed and a seat impure, and still she does not need to count seven clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier, the ברייתא suggested a logical argument that a זב with two sightings should count seven days because he makes a משכב ומושב impure. Here the ברייתא pushes back with a counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed logic was: "whoever makes a bed and seat impure must also count seven." The שומרת יום כנגד יום breaks that link, because she does the first thing but not the second. So the logic cannot be used to make the two-sighting זב count seven.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who bleeds for one or two consecutive days during the eleven days of זיבה. She waits one clean day and then immerses, even after two days of bleeding.
"Will prove": a counterexample that shows an argument does not hold
A bed or seat. These are things meant for lying or sitting, and a זב or זבה makes them impure.
Counting seven clean days before becoming pure

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the גמרא speaking on its own. It is part of a ברייתא that started on the previous amud. The ברייתא first suggested a logical argument and is now knocking it down.

phrases.english: A woman who keeps a day for a day will prove it,
phrases.notes: After one or two days of bleeding, she waits one clean day and then immerses. She is a lighter kind of זבה.

phrases.english: for she makes a bed and a seat impure,
and yet she does not need a count of seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical argument the ברייתא raised on the previous amud
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The logical argument that making a bed and seat impure means you must count seven days
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two laws are not linked. A שומרת יום כנגד יום has the first without the second.

steps.title: The verse teaches that a two-sighting זב counts seven
steps.stepSummary: Since logic would have led us to say he does not count, the ברייתא brings the פסוק ״מִזּוֹבוֹ וְסָפַר״. It teaches that even a זב with only part of the full discharges, meaning two sightings, must count seven clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: So do not be surprised if you would say that he makes a bed and seat impure but still does not count seven. That is why the verse says: "from his discharge, then he shall count." Even part of his discharge leads to counting. This teaches that a זב who saw twice must count seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא admits that, based on the שומרת יום example, we might have concluded that a two-sighting זב does not count. Then it brings a פסוק to teach that he does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ is read as "from his discharge," meaning even part of it. So even a זב who has not reached three sightings is told "and he shall count." The law comes from the פסוק, not from logic.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse comes to say": the opening for a proof from a פסוק
"From his discharge." Here it is read as "part of his discharge."
Part of, some of
A זב who saw two discharges (not three)

steps.whatToRemember: A two-sighting זב must count seven clean days. We know this from the word ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ in the פסוק, not from logic.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that sets the two-sighting זב apart from the שומרת יום. It is also the drasha that רב פפא will question next.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף אַתָּה אַל תִּתְמַהּ עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: And you too, do not be surprised at this,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּטַמֵּא מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב
phrases.english: that even though he makes a bed and seat impure,
phrases.notes: "He" is the זב who saw two discharges.

phrases.english: he should not need a count of seven,
therefore the verse says: "From his discharge, and he shall count,"
even part of his discharge, and he shall count;

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת
phrases.english: this taught about a zav who had two sightings
that he needs a count of seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since logic failed in step 1, the ברייתא brings a פסוק to teach the law
steps.raayaObject: That a two-sighting זב must count seven clean days
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק ״מִזּוֹבוֹ וְסָפַר״, read as "even part of his discharge"

steps.title: רב פפא: how can one word both include and exclude?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי why ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ here includes the two-sighting זב in counting seven, while ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ in the verse about the קרבן excludes him from bringing an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: What is different about this "from his discharge," which we use to include a זב with two sightings? And what is different about that "from his discharge," which we use to exclude a זב with two sightings?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא points out what looks like a contradiction. The same word is read two opposite ways in two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the verse about the offering, ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ is read as a מיעוט: only some זבים bring a קרבן, so the two-sighting זב does not. Here the same word is read as a ריבוי, adding the two-sighting זב to the counting law. רב פפא wants to know what decides which way to read it.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is different?": asking why two similar things are treated differently
Includes; adds a case to the law (ריבוי)
Excludes; leaves a case out of the law (מיעוט)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
What is different about this "from his discharge,"
phrases.notes: This is the one in the counting verse that we just saw.

phrases.aramaic: דִּמְרַבֵּי בֵּיהּ זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: that we include through it a zav with two sightings,
and what is different about that "from his discharge,"
phrases.notes: This is the one in the verse about the זב's offering. There it is used to leave out the two-sighting זב.

phrases.aramaic: דִּמְמַעֵט בֵּיהּ זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת?
phrases.english: that we exclude through it a zav with two sightings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the drasha in step 2 by setting it against the opposite reading in the offering verse
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ as including the two-sighting זב in counting seven
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word is read as excluding him when it comes to the קרבן, so reading it two opposite ways seems inconsistent

steps.title: אביי: an excluding word here would be pointless
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that if ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ in the counting verse were meant to exclude, the פסוק could have just said nothing. Without it, we would never have included the two-sighting זב anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If you think this word came to exclude, then the verse should have stayed silent about it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why, in the counting verse, the word must be read as including the two-sighting זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word that excludes only makes sense if we would otherwise have included the case. In the counting law, nothing would have included the two-sighting זב. So an excluding word would teach nothing. That means the word must be there to include him.

keyTerms.meaning: "If it enters your mind": if you were to think
To exclude
"Let the verse be silent about it": the word would be extra and pointless

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is אביי, answering רב פפא.

phrases.english: If it enters your mind
that this came to exclude,
phrases.notes: "This" is ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ in the counting verse.

phrases.english: let the verse be silent about it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ הַאי לְמַעוֹטֵי הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the word would be extra: an excluding reading would add nothing, so the word must be including
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same word should be read the same way, as excluding, in both places
steps.terutzMaskana: Context decides. Where there was no reason to include the case, an excluding word is pointless, so it must be including.

steps.title: Logic could not include him, as the waiting woman proves
steps.stepSummary: אביי heads off a possible objection: maybe logic would have included the two-sighting זב, so an excluding word was needed. He answers no, because the שומרת יום כנגד יום shows the logic fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that we would have learned it from logic, the woman who waits a day for a day proves that we could not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pictures someone asking whether logic might have included the two-sighting זב. He blocks that by repeating the ברייתא's own counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If logic had included him, an excluding word would have a job to do, and אביי's answer would fall apart. But the שומרת יום כנגד יום already broke that logic in step 1. So only a verse could include him, which is exactly what ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ does.

keyTerms.meaning: "And if you will say": bringing up a possible objection
"It comes from logic": we could work it out by reasoning, without a verse

steps.confusionAlert: The line ״שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם תּוֹכִיחַ״ is a real repeat of step 1. Here אביי uses it for a new purpose: to show logic could never have included the זב, so the verse must be including.
steps.whatToRemember: The two words ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ are not in conflict. For the קרבן it excludes. For counting, there was no other way to include the two-sighting זב, so the word must include him.

phrases.english: And if you will say: it comes from logic,
the woman who keeps a day for a day will prove otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Protects step 4's answer by ruling out the idea that logic would have included the זב
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible claim that logic would have included the two-sighting זב in counting seven
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The שומרת יום כנגד יום makes a bed and seat impure without counting seven, so the logic does not hold

steps.title: Maybe the word is needed for a different lesson
steps.stepSummary: אביי, still answering רב פפא, raises a second possible objection: maybe ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ is needed to teach that the count starts once he is clean of his discharge, even if not of his צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: this word ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ is needed to teach 'from his discharge' and not from his צרעת.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי raises another possible objection to his own answer: maybe the word ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ has a different job. If it does, it would not be free to include the two-sighting זב. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a person who is both a זב and a מצורע. Maybe ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ teaches that he counts his seven days once his discharge stops, even while his צרעת is still there. If so, the proof from steps 2 to 5 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a possible objection
It is needed for: this word has another job
His affliction, meaning his צרעת

phrases.english: And if you would say:
this word is needed for him to teach
'from his discharge' and not from his leprosy,
phrases.notes: He means a person who has both problems. He counts once the discharge stops, even if the צרעת is still there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 5 defended the drasha from the logic side, this raises a new attack: the word may already be used up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ to include the two-sighting זב in counting seven
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the word is needed for a different lesson (from his discharge, not from his צרעת), it cannot also include the two-sighting זב.

steps.title: The verse could have said that without the extra word
steps.stepSummary: The other lesson would already come from ״וְכִי יִטְהַר הַזָּב״. So ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ is extra and teaches that the two-sighting זב counts seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse write 'And when the זב is purified' and stop there. Why do I need ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״? It teaches about a זב with two sightings, that he needs to count seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers this objection and closes the whole discussion. The words 'when the זב is purified' already show it is about the discharge, so ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ is free to teach about the two-sighting זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'When the זב is purified' already speaks of becoming pure from being a זב, which is the discharge, not the צרעת. So the other lesson needs no extra word. Since ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ is extra, it must be teaching something new: that the two-sighting זב also counts seven clean days.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
And let it be silent: the verse could have stopped there
Why do I need it? This points to an extra word
Counting seven clean days

steps.whatToRemember: A זב with only two sightings still counts seven clean days. We learn it from the extra word ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״, not from logic.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write
'And when the zav is purified' and stop there.
Why do I need 'from his discharge'?

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל זָב בַּעַל שְׁתֵּי רְאִיּוֹת
phrases.english: It teaches about a zav with two sightings
that he requires counting seven clean days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 6 and confirms the drasha of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the word is extra: the other lesson already comes from the rest of the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ is used up teaching that he counts from his discharge and not from his צרעת.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'When the זב is purified' already teaches that, so ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״ includes the two-sighting זב in counting seven.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A two-sighting זב must count seven clean days, learned from ״מִזּוֹבוֹ״.

steps.title: Quarantined versus confirmed מצורע while impure
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says the only difference between a מצורע מוסגר and a מצורע מוחלט is letting the hair grow wild and tearing the clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The only difference between a quarantined מצורע and a confirmed מצורע is letting the hair grow wild and tearing the clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, in the same 'אֵין בֵּין' style as the other משניות in this פרק. It compares two kinds of מצורע while they are still impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוסגר is someone whose signs were unclear, so the כהן shut him away to wait and see. A מוחלט was clearly declared a מצורע. Only the מוחלט must let his hair grow wild and tear his clothes. The word 'only' hints that in everything else they are alike.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, our משנה
A quarantined מצורע whose signs were unclear and who waits up to two weeks
A confirmed מצורע whom the כהן declared clearly impure
Letting the hair of the head grow wild
Tearing one's clothes

phrases.english: Mishnah:
There is no difference between a quarantined leper
and a confirmed leper
except letting the hair grow wild and tearing the clothes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין מְצוֹרָע מוּסְגָּר לִמְצוֹרָע מוּחְלָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The זב discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While impure, the only differences between a מוסגר and a מוחלט are פריעה and פרימה, which apply only to the מוחלט.

steps.title: Purified from quarantine versus purified from confirmed צרעת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: when they become pure, the only difference is that the formerly confirmed מצורע must shave and bring birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only difference between one who became pure after quarantine and one who became pure after being confirmed is shaving and the birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה makes a second comparison, this time at the stage of becoming pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוסגר whose signs never became clear just goes free. Only someone who was a confirmed מצורע has to shave his body and bring the two birds for his purification. This is a separate stage from the first comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Quarantine
Being confirmed as a מצורע
Shaving the hair of the body
The two birds used in the מצורע's purification

phrases.english: There is no difference between one purified out of quarantine
and one purified out of confirmed leprosy
except shaving and the birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּין טָהוֹר מִתּוֹךְ הֶסְגֵּר לְטָהוֹר מִתּוֹךְ הֶחְלֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same משנה, moving from the impure stage to the purification stage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When becoming pure, only the formerly confirmed מצורע needs תגלחת and צפרים.

steps.title: Both are sent out and both are impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads into the word 'only' and concludes that a מוסגר and a מוחלט are the same in being sent out and in impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that for being sent out and for impurity, both are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pulling an inference from the משנה's wording. Since the משנה listed only two differences, everything else must be the same, including being sent out of the camp and being impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'אֵין בֵּין... אֶלָּא', meaning the difference is only these things. So the גמרא concludes that a מוסגר is also sent away and is also impure, just like a מוחלט. This inference sets up the discussion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא
Being sent out of the camp, or out of a walled city
This one and that one are equal

steps.confusionAlert: A מוסגר is not 'less impure'. He is fully impure and sent out like a מוחלט. He only skips פריעה, פרימה, and later the shaving and birds.

phrases.english: Gemara:
This implies that regarding being sent out and impurity,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording; some versions don't have it. Either way, the point includes impurity too.

phrases.english: this one and that one are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְעִנְיַן שִׁילּוּחַ וְטוּמְאָה זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the word 'only' in the משנה of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוסגר and a מוחלט are the same in שילוח and טומאה.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn the law from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that only a מצורע מוחלט, and not a מצורע מוסגר, lets his hair grow wild and tears his clothing. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the only difference between a מוסגר and a מוחלט is פריעה and פרימה. The גמרא now wants a פסוק showing that a מוסגר is free from these.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? A request for a source.

phrases.english: From where are these things known?
phrases.notes: He means the rule that a quarantined מצורע does not let his hair grow or tear his clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the difference stated in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a מצורע מוסגר is exempt from פריעה and פרימה.

steps.title: The word 'and he is pure' shows he was free from the start
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק learns from ״וְטָהֵר״ that a מוסגר was never obligated in פריעה and פרימה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב שמואל בר יצחק taught before רב הונא: 'The כהן shall declare him pure, it is a scab, and he shall wash his clothes and be pure.' This means he was pure from the letting-grow and tearing from the very beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר יצחק answers with a פסוק about a מוסגר who is released. The word ״וְטָהֵר״ is read to mean he was 'pure' from the start of פריעה and פרימה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שמואל בר יצחק reads ״וְטָהֵר״ as 'and he is pure,' a status he already had, not one he gains only now. So the word teaches that even during quarantine he was pure of פריעה and פרימה. He never had to let his hair grow or tear his clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Letting the hair of the head grow wild.
Tearing one's clothing.
A scab, a mark that turns out not to be צרעת.
From the beginning.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתָנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: As Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak taught before Rav Huna:
"The priest shall declare him pure; it is a scab,
phrases.notes: This פסוק (ויקרא יג:ו) is about a quarantined person whose mark did not spread, so he is released.

phrases.english: and he shall wash his clothes and be pure."
He is pure from the letting-grow and tearing of the beginning.
phrases.notes: In other words, back when he was quarantined, he never had to let his hair grow or tear his clothes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״וְטָהֵר״ by a released מוסגר teaches he was pure of פריעה and פרימה from the beginning.

steps.title: רבא: the same word appears by a זב
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the reading, since ״וְטָהֵר״ is also said about a זב, who was fully impure before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, by a זב, where it is written 'and he shall wash his clothes and be pure', what 'pure from the beginning' is there?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the proof by pointing to the identical word ״וְטָהֵר״ in the פרשה of זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״וְטָהֵר״ meant 'pure from the beginning,' it would have to mean that by a זב too. But a זב was completely impure until he counted and immersed, so that reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: a phrase that shows a reading leads to a bad result.
A man made impure by a bodily discharge.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: But if so,
regarding a zav, where it is written
phrases.notes: ויקרא טו:יג, about a זב who has finished counting his clean days.

phrases.english: "and he shall wash his clothes and be pure,"
there, what 'pure from the beginning' is there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of ״וְטָהֵר״ as 'pure from the beginning.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word by a זב cannot mean 'pure from the beginning,' so it cannot mean that by the מצורע either.

steps.title: What 'and he is pure' really means by a זב
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ״וְטָהֵר״ by a זב means he is now pure, and a new discharge will not make him impure backwards.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: he is now pure from making clay vessels impure by moving them. Even if he sees another discharge, he does not make them impure retroactively.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own meaning for ״וְטָהֵר״ by a זב. This sets up how he will read the same word by the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב makes a clay vessel impure just by moving it, which is called היסט. The case is a זב who counted seven clean days and immersed on the seventh day, and then had another discharge that same day. That discharge undoes his count and makes beds, seats and people impure retroactively. ״וְטָהֵר״ teaches one narrow exception: clay vessels he moved between the immersion and the new discharge stay pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Moving an item without touching it, which spreads impurity from a זב.
A clay or earthenware vessel.
Backwards in time, retroactively.

phrases.english: Rather: he is pure now
from making an earthenware vessel impure by moving it,
even though he then sees again —
phrases.notes: "Sees" means he has another discharge.

phrases.english: he does not make impure retroactively.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: טָהוֹר הַשְׁתָּא מִלְּטַמֵּא כְּלִי חֶרֶס בְּהֶיסֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא replaces the rejected reading with his own explanation of ״וְטָהֵר״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By a זב, ״וְטָהֵר״ means his immersion on the seventh day still helps for clay vessels he moved: even if he has another discharge that same day, which undoes his count and makes his bed and seat impure retroactively, those vessels stay pure.

steps.title: The same meaning applies to the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: רבא applies his reading to the מצורע, so the word ״וְטָהֵר״ no longer proves anything about פריעה and פרימה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, he is pure now from making things impure by entering, retroactively.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says ״וְטָהֵר״ by the released מוסגר means the same thing as by the זב. That removes the proof of רב שמואל בר יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע makes everything in a house impure just by entering it, called ביאה. ״וְטָהֵר״ teaches that once released, the מוסגר is truly pure. If real צרעת appears later, we do not say he was a מצורע all along and make impure every house he entered. So the פסוק is about this, not about פריעה and פרימה.

keyTerms.meaning: Entering a house; a מצורע makes its contents impure this way.
Here too: the same idea applies to this case.

steps.whatToRemember: רבא reads ״וְטָהֵר״ as 'now fully pure, with no backwards impurity' by both a זב and a מצורע. So ״וְטָהֵר״ cannot be the source for freeing a מוסגר from פריעה and פרימה. The next step gives רבא's new source.

phrases.english: Here too, he is pure
[now, from making things impure by entering, retroactively].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; some versions don't have them. If he later gets real צרעת, houses he entered before stay pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's reading of the זב פסוק to the מצורע, undoing step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב שמואל בר יצחק's proof from ״וְטָהֵר״.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ״וְטָהֵר״ is needed to teach that a released מוסגר causes no backwards impurity by entering houses, so it says nothing about פריעה and פרימה.

steps.title: רבא's new source: the leper 'in whom the plague is'
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from ״וְהַצָּרוּעַ אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ הַנֶּגַע״ that only a מצורע whose צרעת depends on his body does פריעה and פרימה. This leaves out the מוסגר, whose status depends on the passing of days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: we learn it from here. The פסוק says, "And the leper in whom the plague is." That means someone whose צרעת depends on his body. It leaves out this one, whose צרעת does not depend on his body but on days.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the proof from ״וְטָהֵר״ fell apart, רבא offers a brand-new source for why a מוסגר does not do פריעה and פרימה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוחלט is impure because of what is on his body right now. A מוסגר is waiting out a set number of days to see what the mark does, so his status is tied to time. The word ״בּוֹ״ (in him) points only to the first kind.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who has צרעת (a leper)
Depends on his body
Depends on days, meaning the waiting period
From here (introduces a source)

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: from here:
"And the leper in whom the plague is,"
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in ויקרא that goes on to command torn clothes and wild hair.

phrases.english: one whose leprosy depends on his body,
this excludes one whose leprosy
does not depend on his body, but on days.
phrases.notes: He means the מוסגר, who has to wait seven days to see what the mark does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source that was rejected in step 15 with a new one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we learn that a מוסגר is free from פריעה and פרימה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From ״אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ הַנֶּגַע״, which limits the law to a מצורע whose צרעת depends on his body.

steps.title: אביי: then the מוסגר should also be free from being sent out
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that ״בּוֹ״ also appears in the פסוק about being impure and sent out. By רבא's logic, a מוסגר would not need שילוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But if so, the פסוק "All the days during which the plague is in him, he shall be impure" should mean the same thing. Only someone whose צרעת depends on his body needs to be sent out, and someone whose צרעת does not depend on his body does not need to be sent out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא by taking his reading of ״בּוֹ״ and applying it to the very next פסוק, about sending the מצורע out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״בּוֹ״ leaves out the מוסגר in one פסוק, it should leave him out in the next פסוק too. That would mean a מוסגר is not sent out of the camp. אביי is setting up why that result is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (what you said leads to a strange result)
Being sent out of the camp
Requires

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But if so,
"All the days during which the plague is in him, he shall be impure,"
phrases.notes: This is the very next פסוק, which ends with the מצורע living outside the camp. Notice the same word ״בּוֹ״.

phrases.english: one whose leprosy depends on his body
is the one who requires being sent out,
and one whose leprosy does not depend on his body
does not require being sent out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's new reading by applying it to a parallel פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of ״בּוֹ״ as excluding the מוסגר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word in the שילוח פסוק would then exclude the מוסגר from being sent out, which is a result we do not accept.

steps.title: Blocking the escape: the משנה says they are the same for being sent out
steps.stepSummary: If you say a מוסגר really is not sent out, the משנה rules that out. It says the only difference between a מוסגר and a מוחלט is פריעה and פרימה, so for שילוח and making a house impure they are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: yes, that is true, a מוסגר is not sent out. But the משנה teaches: The only difference between a מצורע מוסגר and a מצורע מוחלט is letting the hair grow wild and tearing the clothes. That implies that for being sent out, and for making things impure by coming into a house, both are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes off the easy way out. רבא cannot just accept that a מוסגר is not sent out, because our own משנה says otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording "the only difference is" means everything else is the same. So the מוסגר is sent out and makes a house impure just like a מוחלט. Now רבא needs a source that includes the מוסגר in שילוח.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
Yes, that is indeed so
But isn't it taught
To make things impure just by entering a house

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new attack. It is still אביי's same challenge from step 17, now showing why we cannot simply accept its result.

phrases.english: And if you would say: indeed so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: maybe a מוסגר really is not sent out.

phrases.english: but isn't it taught:
There is no difference between a quarantined leper
and a confirmed leper
except letting the hair grow wild and tearing the clothes.
This implies that regarding being sent out
and making things impure by entering,
this one and that one are the same!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's challenge by showing the result from step 17 goes against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option of accepting that a מוסגר is not sent out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the only difference is פריעה and פרימה, so in שילוח the מוסגר and מוחלט must be the same.

steps.title: רבא: the word 'all' includes the מוסגר in being sent out
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the פסוק could have said ״יְמֵי״ but says ״כׇּל יְמֵי״. The extra word ״כׇּל״ comes to include the מוסגר in שילוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: The פסוק could have said "the days," but it says "all the days." That comes to include a מצורע מוסגר in being sent out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי by finding an extra word in the שילוח פסוק that brings the מוסגר back in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that ״בּוֹ״ by itself would leave out the מוסגר. But in the שילוח פסוק, the extra word ״כׇּל״ adds him back. The פריעה and פרימה פסוק has no such extra word, so there the מוסגר stays left out.

keyTerms.meaning: To include
All the days

steps.whatToRemember: A מוסגר is free from פריעה and פרימה because of ״אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ הַנֶּגַע״, but he is still sent out, because ״כׇּל יְמֵי״ includes him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps רבא's source in line with the משנה: the only difference between מוסגר and מוחלט is פריעה and פרימה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: "He" here is רבא answering אביי.

phrases.english: "The days," "all the days,"
to include a quarantined leper in being sent out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from steps 17-18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the פסוק (ריבוי) overrides the exclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word ״בּוֹ״ in the שילוח פסוק would leave the מוסגר out of being sent out.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״כׇּל״ includes the מוסגר in שילוח, so only פריעה and פרימה stay excluded.

steps.title: Then why no shaving and birds for the quarantined leper?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a מוסגר does not do תגלחת and bring צפרים, since the משנה teaches that these are the only differences in purification between a מוסגר and a מוחלט.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why doesn't a מוסגר do shaving and bring birds? The משנה teaches that the only difference between someone purified from quarantine and someone purified from confirmed צרעת is shaving and birds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the approach it has been building. If the מוסגר is treated like the מוחלט except where a פסוק leaves him out, which פסוק leaves him out of shaving and birds?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, every difference between the מוסגר and the מוחלט needed its own source in a פסוק. The משנה says that when they become pure, they differ only in תגלחת and צפרים. So the גמרא demands a source that leaves the מוסגר out of these two.

keyTerms.meaning: The shaving of all body hair that a cured מצורע does as part of becoming pure
The two birds a cured מצורע brings in his purification process
Quarantine: the waiting period of a person whose signs of צרעת are not yet clear (a מוסגר)
Confirmed צרעת: a person definitely declared a מצורע (a מוחלט)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: If so,
shaving and birds, what is the reason he does not do them?
As the משנה teaches:
There is no difference between one who becomes pure from quarantine
and one who becomes pure from confirmed צרעת
except for shaving and birds!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, תִּגְלַחַת וְצִפֳּרִים מַאי טַעְמָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the approach that every difference between מוסגר and מוחלט needs a source in a פסוק, and asks for the source for the last two differences.
steps.kashyaTarget: The approach that the מוסגר is treated like the מוחלט except where a פסוק excludes him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows the מוסגר does not do תגלחת and צפרים, but so far no פסוק excludes him from them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that excludes the מוסגר from תגלחת and צפרים

steps.title: Shaving and birds are only for leprosy cured by healing
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns from ״וְהִנֵּה נִרְפָּא נֶגַע הַצָּרַעַת״ that תגלחת and צפרים apply only to a מצורע whose cure depends on healing. This leaves out the מוסגר, whose status depends on days.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק says, ״And the כהן shall go out of the camp, and behold, the plague of צרעת is healed.״ This means someone whose צרעת depends on healing. It leaves out the one whose צרעת does not depend on healing but on days.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the source the גמרא asked for. The purification פסוק talks about the צרעת being healed, and that fits only the מוחלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוחלט stays impure until his נגע actually heals, so his purity depends on healing. A מוסגר becomes pure when his days of quarantine end without the signs becoming confirmed, so his purity depends on days. Since the פסוק about shaving and birds is tied to healing, it covers only the מוחלט.

keyTerms.meaning: Was healed
Depends on healing
By days, meaning by the passing of time

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא learned each difference between a מוסגר and a מוחלט from a פסוק. ״בּוֹ״ leaves the מוסגר out of פריעה and פרימה. ״כׇּל״ brings him back in for שילוח. ״נִרְפָּא״ leaves him out of תגלחת and צפרים, because his purity depends on days, not on healing.

phrases.english: אביי said:
The verse says:
"And the priest shall go out of the camp
phrases.notes: This is the start of the פסוק about how a מצורע becomes pure, which includes the shaving and the birds.

phrases.english: and behold, the plague of צרעת is healed,"
this means one whose צרעת depends on healing.
This leaves out the one whose צרעת does not depend
on healing but on days.
phrases.notes: That is the מוסגר: he becomes pure when his quarantine days end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by giving the missing source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a פסוק that excludes the מוסגר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No פסוק excludes the מוסגר from shaving and birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״נִרְפָּא״ limits shaving and birds to a מצורע whose cure depends on healing, which leaves out the מוסגר.

steps.title: New משנה: ספרים versus תפילין ומזוזות
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that ספרים may be written in any language, while תפילין ומזוזות must be written only in אשורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The only difference between ספרים and תפילין ומזוזות is this: ספרים may be written in any language, while תפילין ומזוזות may only be written in אשורית.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins in the same "there is no difference except" pattern. It compares how ספרים are written with how תפילין ומזוזות are written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives only one difference: the language and script allowed. ספרים can be written in any language and still be holy. תפילין ומזוזות must be in Hebrew, in the Hebrew square script. Since it says this is the only difference, it suggests that in other writing rules they are alike.

keyTerms.meaning: Scrolls of the books of תנ״ך, such as a ספר תורה
Tefillin and mezuzos
In any language
The Hebrew language written in the Hebrew square script
The משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Here "ספרים" does not mean books in general. It means holy scrolls of תנ״ך, mainly a ספר תורה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: There is no difference between scrolls
and tefillin and mezuzos,
except that scrolls may be written in any language,
while tefillin and mezuzos may not be written
except in Ashurit.
phrases.notes: He means Hebrew, written in the square Hebrew letters we use today.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין בֵּין סְפָרִים לִתְפִלִּין וּמְזוּזוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the מצורע discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספרים may be written in any language; תפילין ומזוזות only in אשורית.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: scrolls only in Greek
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees and says that even ספרים were only permitted to be written in Greek, besides Hebrew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Even for ספרים, the חכמים only permitted them to be written in Greek.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the משנה narrows the first ruling. Not every language is allowed for ספרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion allows ספרים in any language. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the only other language permitted is Greek. A scroll in any other language would not have the holiness of a ספר.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not permit
Greek

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even for scrolls, they did not permit
that they be written except in Greek.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אַף בִּסְפָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה about which languages are allowed for ספרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספרים may be written only in Hebrew or Greek, not in any other language.

steps.title: Inference: in sewing and in making hands impure, ספרים and תפילין are the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that ספרים and תפילין ומזוזות are equal in two ways: both are sewn with sinews, and both make the hands טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: This implies that for sewing them with sinews, and for making the hands impure, both are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by reading between the lines of the משנה. Since the משנה names only one difference, every other rule must be shared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the only difference between ספרים and תפילין ומזוזות is the language rule. So the גמרא concludes that in other areas they are equal. Both must be sewn with sinews, and the רבנן's decree that holy scrolls make the hands טמא applies to both.

keyTerms.meaning: Sinews (animal tendons), used as thread to sew the parchment sheets together
To make the hands impure. This is a decree of the רבנן about touching holy scrolls
This one and that one are equal
This implies. It signals that the גמרא is drawing an inference

phrases.english: GEMARA:
This implies that for sewing them with sinews,
and for making the hands impure,
this and that are equal.
phrases.notes: 'This' means ספרים, and 'that' means תפילין and מזוזות.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לְתוֹפְרָן בְּגִידִין וּלְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the new משנה from steps 22–23 by drawing an inference from its 'only difference' wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Apart from language, ספרים and תפילין ומזוזות are equal: both are sewn with sinews, and both make the hands טמא.

steps.title: Contradiction: a ברייתא says a scroll in another language or script is not holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the משנה's rule that ספרים may be written in any language against a ברייתא. The ברייתא says a scroll makes the hands טמא only if it is written in אשורית, on parchment, and in ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Scrolls are written in any language,' etc. But a ברייתא contradicts this: A Bible verse written in Aramaic translation, an Aramaic translation written in Bible Hebrew, or anything in the old Hebrew script does not make the hands impure. It only does so once it is written in אשורית script, on a scroll, and in ink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and then brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats a ספר in any language as a real, holy ספר. The ברייתא says a scroll in תרגום or in כתב עברי does not make the hands טמא. That suggests it lacks the holiness of a ספר. So the question is how a ספר written in another language can count as holy.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set it against… This introduces a contradiction from another source
The original Hebrew text of the תנ״ך
The Aramaic translation
The ancient Hebrew script, as opposed to אשורית
The square script that ספרי תורה are written in

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up language with script. כתב עברי is still the Hebrew language, but written in the old letters. The ברייתא says even that is not enough. It must be in אשורית letters.

phrases.english: 'And scrolls are written in any language,' etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה from step 22.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
A Bible verse that one wrote in Aramaic translation,
or an Aramaic translation that one wrote in Bible Hebrew,
phrases.notes: This means the Aramaic sections of תנ״ך, like parts of דניאל, written in Hebrew instead.

phrases.english: or one written in the old Hebrew script —
does not make the hands impure,
until one writes it in אשורית script,
on a scroll, and in ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After drawing the inference about what ספרים share with תפילין, the גמרא now challenges the one difference the משנה did name, the language rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that ספרים may be written in any language.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that a scroll in תרגום or in כתב עברי does not make the hands טמא, which implies it is not holy. That clashes with the משנה, which accepts ספרים in any language.

steps.title: רבא begins his answer: there is no contradiction
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens his answer by saying the contradiction is not a real difficulty. His explanation follows on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא announces that he can resolve the contradiction. This line is a setup, and his actual explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא קשיא' signals that the משנה and the ברייתא do not truly conflict. Usually this means the two sources are talking about different cases. Watch for how רבא divides them on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This announces that a contradiction can be resolved

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds directly to the contradiction raised in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Opening of a resolution. The details are not yet given on this amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seem to disagree about whether a ספר in another language is holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pending: רבא's explanation continues on the next amud.
